summary: Exeter lookout: a 1917 wooden tower replaced in 1946 by a 65-foot steel tower, on the NHLR since 2014; standing and unstaffed, with power reconnected in 2022.

facts.design: 65-foot steel tower that replaced a 1917 wooden lookout on the same site

access.note: Administered by Rhode Island DEM. The 2016 visit report found the lower stairs removed. The sources give no public access rules.

visit.trail_note: As of the 2016 visit the lower stairs were gone and trees and vines covered the legs of the tower, which makes climbing from the ground unlikely. No later visit report was found, and no source says whether the public may climb.

facts.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

events.note: Original wooden lookout tower built on the site.
A 1918 state forestry report describes a 50-foot wood tower with an observer.
Mrs. Hope Andrews, the sixth woman to be fire warden there, on duty 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Kingston Daily Freeman, August 30, 1939, as quoted by Forest Lookouts).
Wooden tower replaced with the current 65-foot steel tower. The register's Built field gives 1946.
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: September 3, 2014 (US 1044, RI 6).
Visit report, November 20, 2016: okay condition for its lack of maintenance; lower stairs removed; trees and vines around the legs; every step and landing is grated steel.

Small group of ham radio operators and former or current emergency personnel reconnected power to Pine Hill in Exeter, as part of a statewide effort to restore many of the state's remaining fire towers. The report does not say the group restored this tower itself.

corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height of the 1917 wooden tower in the 1918 report. The register describes the current tower as 65-foot steel, built 1946.

corrections.proposed: 1917 wooden tower built; 1946 replaced with the current 65-foot steel tower
corrections.why: The register says the original wooden tower was built in 1917 and replaced in 1946. The 1946 date belongs to the current steel tower, not the first tower on the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1918 report gives 543 feet above sea level. The register gives 540 ft (165 m). The difference is small and the story uses the register figure.

sources.title: Forest Fire Lookout Association 2022 regional report (PDF)

notes_for_editor: Brief's restored 2022 was narrowed to reconnected power, which is what the FFLA 2022 report names for Pine Hill. The report describes general restoration work across the state, not a restoration of this tower. The brief's height 15.2 m is the 1917 wooden tower's height and is corrected to the current 65-foot steel tower. Staffing status 'unstaffed' rests on the register's Staffed? field alone. The 2016 visit is the only condition report. No source read states current public access, and the search results for an Arcadia or RI DEM access page did not mention the tower. Two search results for Pine Hill (a directory listing for an address on Gardiner Rd, and a mapcarta entry) were not read and are not used.
